newsitem.title: BELARUS: Russia's Slavneft to modernise Mozyr refinery.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Slavneft to modernise Mozyr refinery.

text.p: Russian-Belarussian joint venture Slavneft will begin to modernise its Mozyr oil refinery in Belarus in the first quarter of 1997, the head of the company said on Monday.
"We started the first investment this year. More than $4 million has been invested in a project to reconstruct the facility," Slavneft President Anatoly Fomin told a news conference.
Fomin said the initial phase of upgrading the facility is being carried out by St Petersburg-based Neftekhimproyekt and Metallgesellschaft AG's Lurgi AG.

It will cost $150 million to modernise the facility, half the original estimate of $300 million, Fomin said. "We were forced to work out a new plan, due to the sharp reduction in the size of the financing," he explained.

Slavneft is a vertically-integrated oil company which is 80 percent owned by the Russian government. It has a 43 percent stake in Mozyr and its main production unit is AOOT Megionneftegaz MFGS.RTS 0#MFGS.RUO .
Fomin also announced that Slavneft will supply 3.5 million tonnes of oil to Mozyr for processing in 1997. He said Slavneft might grant Belarussia trade credits to help it carry out its spring sowing.
He said Slavneft had granted $100 million worth of trade credits to Belarussia in 1996, but there had been problems with repayment.
